project.name: claude-code-api-service
project.description: API wrapper around the Claude Code CLI for rapid prototyping: a FastAPI service that routes/proxies LLM requests through the Claude Code CLI with tool passthrough, plus a Typer CLI and a Python client library (port 8006)

nodes.name: middleware.py
nodes.summary: Defines the request-id middleware that mints/propagates X-Request-ID and an OpenTelemetry span processor that stamps the request id onto active spans.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines a Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware subclass with an OpenTelemetry SpanProcessor that reads a contextvar.

nodes.name: RequestIDMiddleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware that honors an inbound X-Request-ID or mints a UUID, stores it in a contextvar, and emits it on both request and response headers.

nodes.name: CCARequestIdSpanProcessor
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry SpanProcessor that sets the current request id as a span attribute when a span starts and recording is active.

nodes.name: settings.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic settings module centralizing service configuration (host/port, Redis, model defaults, budget, timeouts, and feature flags) loaded from environment variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pydantic BaseSettings to bind environment variables to typed configuration fields.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Pydantic settings class with 16 typed configuration fields covering server, Redis, model, budget, and timeout settings sourced from the environment.

nodes.name: tool_translation.py
nodes.summary: Pure translation helpers converting OpenAI-style tools, messages, and tool_choice into the Anthropic format and converting Anthropic tool results back into OpenAI responses.

nodes.name: openai_tools_to_anthropic
nodes.summary: Converts an OpenAI function-tool list into the Anthropic tool schema format.

nodes.name: openai_messages_to_anthropic
nodes.summary: Translates OpenAI chat messages (including tool calls and tool results) into Anthropic message/content-block format.

nodes.name: openai_tool_choice_to_anthropic
nodes.summary: Maps an OpenAI tool_choice directive to the equivalent Anthropic tool_choice setting.

nodes.name: anthropic_result_to_openai_response
nodes.summary: Converts an Anthropic tool/result message into an OpenAI-style chat completion response with tool_calls.

nodes.name: worker_pool.py
nodes.summary: Asynchronous worker pool that runs Claude Code CLI tasks as subprocesses with concurrency limits, queuing, timeouts, cost calculation, PID tracking, and CLI-stderr error classification.
nodes.languageNotes: Manages asyncio subprocesses with bounded concurrency and a queue; TaskStatus is an Enum and TaskResult/Task are dataclasses.

nodes.name: _classify_cli_stderr
nodes.summary: Classifies Claude Code CLI stderr output into a structured error category for downstream HTTP mapping.

nodes.name: TaskResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a completed task's status, output, error, usage, cost, and content blocks (with tool-passthrough backward compatibility).

nodes.name: Task
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a submitted task: id, prompt, model, options, timeout, tools, and lifecycle metadata.

nodes.name: WorkerPool
nodes.summary: Core scheduler that submits tasks, runs them as CLI subprocesses under a concurrency limit, queues overflow, enforces timeouts, computes cost, tracks PIDs, and supports kill/cleanup.

nodes.name: test_api.py
nodes.summary: Endpoint tests for the FastAPI app covering chat completion success/auto-model/budget/failure paths, batch processing, usage, model routing, budget enforcement, and health/root.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FastAPI TestClient with mocked worker pool, budget manager, and auth fixtures.

nodes.name: test_basic.py
nodes.summary: Smoke tests verifying the root, health, docs, and OpenAPI schema endpoints respond correctly.

nodes.name: test_cache.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for RedisCache covering cache get/set, TTL expiration, queue operations, error handling, JSON encode/decode failures, clear, and connection checks with a mocked Redis.

nodes.name: test_circuit_breaker.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for CircuitBreaker covering state transitions (closed/open/half-open), failure thresholds, reset on success, and timeout behavior.

nodes.name: test_direct_completion.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for DirectCompletionClient covering CLI-stderr error classification, prompt caching, and that completion calls send cache markers.

nodes.name: test_error_classification.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for CLI-stderr error classification and the error-to-HTTP-status mapping used by the API layer.

nodes.name: test_error_tracker.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for ErrorTracker verifying error recording, rollups, recent-error retrieval, and bounded history.

nodes.name: test_middleware.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the request-id middleware (header emission and inbound id honoring) and the OpenTelemetry span processor's attribute-setting and no-op behaviors.

nodes.name: test_tool_passthrough_phase1.py
nodes.summary: Phase-1 tool-passthrough tests covering TaskResult backward compatibility, direct-completion tool handling, AIServiceResponse content blocks, and adapter conversions.

nodes.name: test_tool_passthrough_phase3.py
nodes.summary: Phase-3 tool-passthrough tests covering OpenAI-to-Anthropic tool/message/tool_choice translation and Anthropic-result-to-OpenAI response conversion.

nodes.name: test_websocket.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the websocket streaming path covering connection, streaming responses, error handling, multi-message sessions, cost calculation, and integration.

nodes.name: test_worker_pool.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for WorkerPool covering submission, concurrency, execution success, timeouts, task kill, queueing, PID tracking, cleanup, cost calculation, and failure handling.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point: wires the lifespan that initializes auth, cache, worker pool, budget, websocket and observability, mounts the API routers, and exposes health/ready/root/stream endpoints.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FastAPI's async lifespan context manager to manage startup/shutdown of all platform singletons; OpenTelemetry instrumentation is set up here.

nodes.name: lifespan
nodes.summary: Async lifespan handler that initializes and tears down auth, Redis cache, worker pool, budget manager, permission manager, websocket streamer, and telemetry for the FastAPI app.

nodes.name: health
nodes.summary: Health endpoint aggregating the status of cache, worker pool, auth, and downstream dependencies into a HealthResponse.

nodes.name: ready
nodes.summary: Readiness probe reporting whether the service has finished initialization and can accept traffic.

nodes.name: root
nodes.summary: Root endpoint returning service metadata and available routes.

nodes.name: stream
nodes.summary: Streaming endpoint stub that delegates streamed completions to the websocket/streamer path.

nodes.name: ServiceHealth
nodes.summary: Pydantic model describing the health of a single dependent service (name and status).

nodes.name: HealthResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model for the health endpoint, carrying overall status and per-service health entries.

nodes.name: ReadyResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model for the readiness probe (ready flag and reason).

nodes.name: api.py
nodes.summary: Primary API router defining chat completion (CLI and tool-passthrough paths), batch processing, usage, model routing, an ai-service-compatible endpoint, provider listing, agentic task execution, and capabilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Large APIRouter combining many Pydantic request/response models with endpoint handlers; delegates to worker pool, budget manager, model router, and the agentic executor.

nodes.name: _raise_for_failed_task
nodes.summary: Maps a failed worker-pool TaskResult to the appropriate HTTP error response, classifying error categories.

nodes.name: initialize_services
nodes.summary: Injects the worker pool, budget manager, auth, and permission manager singletons into the router module so handlers can use them.

nodes.name: chat_completion
nodes.summary: Chat completion entry handler that dispatches to the CLI or tool-passthrough completion path based on request shape.

nodes.name: _chat_completion_cli
nodes.summary: Runs a chat completion through the Claude Code CLI worker pool, enforcing budget and shaping the ChatCompletionResponse.

nodes.name: _chat_completion_with_tools
nodes.summary: Handles tool-passthrough chat completions via the direct completion client, translating tool definitions and assembling the response.

nodes.name: batch_processing
nodes.summary: Processes a batch of prompts concurrently through the worker pool, aggregating per-item results, costs, and tokens.

nodes.name: get_usage
nodes.summary: Returns project usage statistics for a period from the budget manager, broken down by model.

nodes.name: route_recommendation
nodes.summary: Recommends a Claude model for a task using the model router, factoring in budget and task characteristics.

nodes.name: process_ai_services_compatible
nodes.summary: AI-service-compatible endpoint adapting an external request format to the Claude completion path and converting the response back, with tool support.

nodes.name: list_providers
nodes.summary: Lists the supported model providers exposed by the service.

nodes.name: get_provider_models
nodes.summary: Returns the available models for a given provider.

nodes.name: execute_agentic_task
nodes.summary: Runs an agentic task through the AgenticExecutor, enforcing budget and returning the execution log and artifacts.

nodes.name: get_capabilities
nodes.summary: Reports the service capabilities, including available agents and skills, as a CapabilitiesResponse.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Pydantic chat message model (role, content, and optional tool fields).

nodes.name: ChatCompletionRequest
nodes.summary: Pydantic request model for chat completions, including messages, model, tools, and generation parameters.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Pydantic token-usage model (prompt, completion, total tokens).

nodes.name: ChatCompletionResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model for chat completions, carrying id, model, choices/content, usage, and cost.

nodes.name: BatchPrompt
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a single prompt within a batch request.

nodes.name: BatchRequest
nodes.summary: Pydantic request model wrapping a list of batch prompts plus shared options.

nodes.name: BatchResult
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a single batch item's outcome (status, content, usage, cost, error).

nodes.name: BatchResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model aggregating batch results with totals and cumulative cost/tokens.

nodes.name: RouteRequest
nodes.summary: Pydantic request model for a model-routing recommendation (task description and constraints).

nodes.name: RouteResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model carrying the recommended model and rationale.

nodes.name: UsageByModel
nodes.summary: Pydantic model holding per-model usage figures.

nodes.name: UsageResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model for the usage endpoint with totals and per-model breakdown.

nodes.name: AgentListItem
nodes.summary: Pydantic model describing an available agent in the capabilities response.

nodes.name: SkillListItem
nodes.summary: Pydantic model describing an available skill in the capabilities response.

nodes.name: CapabilitiesResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model listing service capabilities, agents, and skills.

nodes.name: cache.py
nodes.summary: Redis-backed cache and queue abstraction providing get/set with TTL, queue push/pop, clear, and connection management for the service.

nodes.name: RedisCache
nodes.summary: Wraps a Redis connection to provide JSON cache get/set with TTL, FIFO queue operations, clear, connection checks, and graceful degradation when disconnected.

nodes.name: circuit_breaker.py
nodes.summary: Implements a circuit breaker that trips after repeated failures and transitions through closed/open/half-open states to protect downstream calls.

nodes.name: CircuitBreaker
nodes.summary: State machine that counts failures, opens the circuit on threshold breach, allows trial calls in half-open state, and resets on success.

nodes.name: compatibility_adapter.py
nodes.summary: Adapter translating an external ai-service request/response format to and from the Claude message format, including model mapping and message conversion.

nodes.name: map_model_to_claude
nodes.summary: Maps an external/legacy model identifier to the corresponding Claude model name.

nodes.name: convert_to_messages
nodes.summary: Converts an external ProcessRequest into the Claude messages format, handling roles and content blocks.

nodes.name: convert_response
nodes.summary: Converts a Claude completion result back into the external AIServiceResponse format, including content blocks.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Dataclass for an external-format message with role and content fields.

nodes.name: ProcessRequest
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing the full external ai-service request (messages, model, tools, and generation options).

nodes.name: AIServiceResponse
nodes.summary: Dataclass for the external ai-service response format with content, usage, and metadata.

nodes.name: direct_completion.py
nodes.summary: Direct completion client that calls the Claude Code CLI worker pool for tool-passthrough completions, with prompt caching and CLI-stderr error classification.

nodes.name: DirectCompletionClient
nodes.summary: Issues direct completions through the worker pool with tool support, prompt-cache markers, and structured error classification from CLI output.

nodes.name: error_tracker.py
nodes.summary: In-memory error tracker that records recent errors with timestamps and exposes summaries for health and observability.

nodes.name: ErrorTracker
nodes.summary: Records and rolls up recent error entries, exposing counts and recent-error queries for the health endpoint.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands managing the service process lifecycle: start, stop, restart, status, install/uninstall a launchd plist, and tail filtered logs.
nodes.languageNotes: Tracks the service PID in a local file and generates a macOS launchd plist for install.

nodes.name: get_service_pid
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the persisted service PID from the local PID file.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the service process (foreground or background) on a port, optionally checking dependencies and streaming logs.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the running service process, optionally force-killing after a timeout.

nodes.name: restart
nodes.summary: Restarts the service by stopping then starting it on the given port.

nodes.name: status
nodes.summary: Reports whether the service is running, its PID, port, and reachability, in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: _build_plist
nodes.summary: Builds the macOS launchd plist XML used to install the service as a managed agent.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the service as a launchd agent on a port and optionally starts it immediately.

nodes.name: uninstall
nodes.summary: Removes the installed launchd agent for the service.

nodes.name: _tail_logs
nodes.summary: Tails the service log file with optional follow, level, and search filtering.

nodes.name: _matches_filter
nodes.summary: Decides whether a raw log line matches the configured level and search filters.

nodes.name: logs
nodes.summary: CLI command exposing filtered log tailing for the service.

nodes.name: tasks.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands for inspecting and managing asynchronous tasks: list, get, cancel, and view logs.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Lists tasks filtered by status with an optional limit, in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches and renders a single task by id.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Cancels a task by id.

nodes.name: logs
nodes.summary: Displays execution logs for a task by id.

nodes.name: test.py
nodes.summary: CLI self-test commands exercising completion, agentic task, agent/skill discovery, processing, and an aggregate all-in-one suite against the service.

nodes.name: completion
nodes.summary: Tests a chat completion round-trip for a given model and prompt.

nodes.name: task
nodes.summary: Tests submitting an agentic task with selected tools and reports the outcome.

nodes.name: agents
nodes.summary: Tests the agent discovery endpoints.

nodes.name: skills
nodes.summary: Tests the skill discovery endpoints.

nodes.name: process_test
nodes.summary: Tests the single-prompt processing path through service or CLI.

nodes.name: all
nodes.summary: Runs the full battery of self-tests and reports an aggregate pass/fail summary.

nodes.name: usage.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands reporting token/cost usage with breakdowns by period, project, and model, plus export.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Renders an aggregate usage summary for a time period in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: by_project
nodes.summary: Renders usage broken down by project.

nodes.name: export
nodes.summary: Exports usage data to a file in the chosen format.

nodes.name: workers.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands for inspecting and managing the service worker pool: status, list, clear queue, and kill.

nodes.name: status
nodes.summary: Reports worker-pool status and queue depth in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines CLI/service configuration dataclasses and a ConfigManager that detects the service directory and loads/saves config.

nodes.name: ConfigManager
nodes.summary: Resolves the active service directory, validates it, and loads/saves the merged CLI and service configuration.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared CLI presentation helpers: an OutputFormatter plus Rich-based print, table, formatting, spinner, and confirm utilities.

nodes.name: OutputFormatter
nodes.summary: Formats data as table or other output forms for consistent CLI rendering.

nodes.name: format_duration
nodes.summary: Formats a seconds value into a human-readable duration string.

nodes.name: create_status_table
nodes.summary: Builds a Rich status table from a list of items.

nodes.name: create_data_table
nodes.summary: Builds a Rich data table from columns and rows with optional column styling.

nodes.name: api_client.py
nodes.summary: HTTP client wrapper around the claude-code-api-service REST endpoints, providing typed methods for health, chat completion, tasks, usage, providers, batch, and routing.

nodes.name: APIError
nodes.summary: Exception type raised when an API request to the service fails.

nodes.name: APIClient
nodes.summary: REST client exposing get/post/delete plus high-level helpers (chat_completion, create_task, get_usage, batch_process, route_recommend) against the local service.

nodes.name: claude_api.py
nodes.summary: Top-level Typer CLI entry point that assembles all sub-command groups and defines version, config-show, and config-validate commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Typer app composition: each imported command module is registered as a sub-command group.

nodes.name: config_show
nodes.summary: Displays the resolved CLI/service configuration in a formatted panel.

nodes.name: config_validate
nodes.summary: Validates the current configuration and reports detected service directory and reachability.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Root Typer callback handling global flags like verbose before dispatching to sub-commands.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package initializer marking cli/commands as a Python package of CLI sub-command modules.

nodes.name: batch.py
nodes.summary: CLI command for submitting batch prompt-processing requests to the service and rendering results.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Reads prompts from args or file, submits a batch processing request via APIClient, and prints per-prompt results.

nodes.name: discovery.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands for discovering available agents and skills, including search and per-item detail views.

nodes.name: list_agents
nodes.summary: Lists agents available from the service, optionally filtered by model, in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: agent_info
nodes.summary: Fetches and renders detailed metadata for a single agent by name.

nodes.name: search_agents
nodes.summary: Searches agents by free-text query and displays matches.

nodes.name: list_skills
nodes.summary: Lists skills available from the service in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: skill_info
nodes.summary: Fetches and renders detailed metadata for a single skill by name.

nodes.name: search_skills
nodes.summary: Searches skills by free-text query and displays matches.

nodes.name: deps
nodes.summary: Inspects external dependencies (redis, subprocesses) and reports their availability.

nodes.name: ping
nodes.summary: Pings the service liveness or readiness endpoint and reports the result.

nodes.name: keys.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands for managing API keys: create, list, revoke, set permissions, provision, and a local key store on disk.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges the CLI to src/auth.AuthManager and src/permission_manager.PermissionManager; persists keys to a local key-store path (values never logged).

nodes.name: _save_key
nodes.summary: Persists a generated key plus metadata to the local key store file.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Generates a new API key for a project with a permission profile and rate limit, optionally saving it locally.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Lists known API keys with status and metadata, optionally active-only or as JSON.

nodes.name: revoke
nodes.summary: Revokes an API key after optional confirmation.

nodes.name: permissions
nodes.summary: Views or updates the permission profile and cost cap associated with a key.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Validates that a given key authenticates successfully against the service.

nodes.name: provision
nodes.summary: Provisions a key for a service id idempotently, reusing or creating then storing it locally.

nodes.name: get_key
nodes.summary: Retrieves a stored key for a service id from the local key store for scripting use.

nodes.name: store_list
nodes.summary: Lists service ids and metadata present in the local key store.

nodes.name: process.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands for sending a single prompt to a provider/model and for a connectivity self-test of the processing path.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Sends a prompt with optional system message and provider/model selection, rendering the response or JSON.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: Runs a minimal end-to-end processing test against the service or CLI path.

nodes.name: providers.py
nodes.summary: CLI commands listing available LLM providers and the models each provider exposes.

nodes.name: list_providers
nodes.summary: Lists configured LLM providers in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: models
nodes.summary: Lists models for a given provider in table or JSON form.

nodes.name: route.py
nodes.summary: CLI command that asks the service to recommend an optimal model for a prompt given context size.

nodes.name: recommend
nodes.summary: Requests a model routing recommendation for a prompt and renders the suggested model and rationale.

nodes.name: token_tracker_usage.py
nodes.summary: Runnable examples demonstrating TokenTracker parsing/cost calculation and its integration with BudgetManager for usage tracking and budget checks.

nodes.name: example_integration_with_budget_manager
nodes.summary: Demonstrates wiring TokenTracker output into BudgetManager: sets a budget, parses simulated Claude outputs, tracks usage, and prints aggregate statistics.

nodes.name: example_budget_checking
nodes.summary: Demonstrates budget enforcement by tracking usage and calling check_budget to show allowed vs blocked decisions.

nodes.name: example_basic_usage
nodes.summary: Demonstrates parsing a Claude CLI JSON output into structured token-usage and cost data.

nodes.name: example_cost_comparison
nodes.summary: Compares estimated per-model costs for a fixed token count across model tiers.

nodes.name: agent_discovery.py
nodes.summary: Discovers Claude Code agents and skills from the local ~/.claude directory, parses their metadata, and builds prompt sections plus validation helpers used by the agentic executor.

nodes.name: AgentSkillDiscovery
nodes.summary: Scans agent and skill directories, parses agent markdown frontmatter and skill.json metadata, caches results, and builds agent/skill prompt sections plus name-validation maps.

nodes.name: AgentInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a discovered agent's name, description, allowed tools, model, and source file path.

nodes.name: SkillInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a discovered skill's name, description, command, user-interface type, and source file path.

nodes.name: agentic_executor.py
nodes.summary: Core orchestration engine that validates agentic task requests, auto-selects a model, enforces budgets, builds an agent/skill-aware prompt, dispatches work to the worker pool, and collects results, logs, and artifacts.

nodes.name: AgenticExecutor
nodes.summary: Runs an agentic task end-to-end: request validation, model auto-selection, token estimation, budget check, prompt construction, async submission to the WorkerPool, usage tracking, and artifact collection.

nodes.name: AgenticTaskRequest
nodes.summary: Pydantic model describing an agentic task request: description, allowed tools/agents/skills, working directory, timeout, max cost, model, and credentials.

nodes.name: AgenticTaskResponse
nodes.summary: Pydantic response model for an agentic task: task id, status, result, execution log, artifacts, and usage.

nodes.name: ExecutionLogEntry
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a single execution-log step with step number, timestamp, action, and details.

nodes.name: Artifact
nodes.summary: Pydantic model describing a workspace artifact produced by a task: type, path, byte size, and creation time.

nodes.name: audit_logger.py
nodes.summary: Async SQLite-backed audit logger that records tool calls, file access, bash commands, agent spawns, skill invocations, and security events, with query and analytics helpers plus security alerting.

nodes.name: AuditLogger

tour.title: Service Entry Point
tour.description: Start here: main.py is the FastAPI application's entry point and the single place where the whole service is wired together. Its async lifespan handler boots every platform singleton in order — auth, the Redis cache, the worker pool, the budget manager, the permission manager, and the WebSocket streamer — then mounts the API routers and exposes health, readiness, and root probes. Reading this file gives you a bird's-eye map of the eight layers the rest of the tour explores, since every dependency named in the lifespan reappears downstream.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's async lifespan context manager (@asynccontextmanager) replaces the older @app.on_event startup/shutdown hooks: code before `yield` runs at startup, code after runs at shutdown, so all long-lived singletons are constructed and torn down in one place.

tour.title: Configuration & Settings
tour.description: Before tracing a request, understand how the service is configured. settings.py centralizes every tunable — host/port (8006), Redis connection, default model, budget caps, subprocess timeouts, and feature flags — into a single typed Settings object loaded from environment variables. The lifespan from Step 1 reads these values to size the worker pool and budget limits, so this file is the contract between the deployment environment and the running service.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic BaseSettings binds environment variables to typed fields automatically, giving validated, defaulted configuration with no manual os.environ parsing — the Python equivalent of a strongly-typed config schema.

tour.title: The API Router
tour.description: src/api.py is the heart of the request surface: a large FastAPI router defining chat completion (both the CLI and tool-passthrough paths), batch processing, usage reporting, model-routing recommendations, an ai-service-compatible endpoint, provider listing, agentic task execution, and a capabilities endpoint. Every inbound HTTP request lands in a handler here, which then delegates downward to the governance and worker-pool layers from the following steps. This is where the request lifecycle spine truly begins after main.py hands off.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI APIRouter lets you declare endpoints in a separate module and mount them onto the app, while Pydantic request/response models on each handler give automatic request validation and OpenAPI docs generation for free.

tour.title: Authentication & Budget Governance
tour.description: Building on the router from Step 3, every request first passes through governance. auth.py's AuthManager generates, validates, rate-limits, and revokes API keys backed by SQLite and exposes a FastAPI dependency that verifies the request key. budget_manager.py then enforces per-project and global spend limits, recording token usage and cost so a request can be rejected before it ever reaches a subprocess. These two SQLite-backed gatekeepers (fan-in 7 and 9 respectively) are the first half of the 'govern the request' stage.

tour.title: Permissions & Security Validation
tour.description: The second half of governance constrains WHAT a request may do. permission_manager.py defines permission profiles and validates agentic task requests against allowed agents, tools, skills, and resource/cost caps, all stored in SQLite. security_validator.py is the last line of defense before the CLI subprocess runs: it screens shell commands for dangerous patterns, validates file paths against blocked and sensitive locations, and sanitizes environment variables. Together with Step 4 these complete the governance layer that protects a service whose whole job is shelling out to a powerful CLI.

tour.title: The Worker Pool — Subprocess Core
tour.description: This is the architectural keystone: src/worker_pool.py has the highest import fan-in (13) because every request that survives governance flows through it. The WorkerPool runs each Claude Code CLI task as an asyncio subprocess under a bounded concurrency limit, queuing overflow, enforcing timeouts, computing cost, tracking PIDs for kill/cleanup, and classifying CLI stderr into structured error categories. Understanding this file is understanding how CCA actually does its work — it is a subprocess orchestrator wrapping the Claude Code CLI, not a direct LLM client.
tour.languageLesson: Python's asyncio.create_subprocess_exec plus an asyncio.Semaphore lets a single event loop supervise many concurrent CLI processes with bounded parallelism — awaiting process output without blocking, while a queue holds tasks that exceed the concurrency cap.

tour.title: Completion Paths — CLI & Tool Passthrough
tour.description: The router from Step 3 dispatches completions down two roads that both end at the worker pool from Step 6. direct_completion.py issues tool-passthrough completions with prompt-cache markers and structured error classification, while tool_translation.py provides the pure functions that convert OpenAI-style tools, messages, and tool_choice into the Anthropic format and translate Anthropic tool results back into OpenAI responses. This adapter pair is why CCA can accept OpenAI-shaped tool requests yet drive the Anthropic-native Claude Code CLI underneath.

tour.title: Agentic Execution & Model Routing
tour.description: Beyond single completions, CCA can run multi-step agentic tasks. agentic_executor.py is the orchestration engine: it validates an agentic request, auto-selects a model, enforces budgets, builds an agent/skill-aware prompt, dispatches to the worker pool from Step 6, and collects the execution log and artifacts. model_router.py supports it by heuristically picking a Claude tier (haiku/sonnet/opus) from prompt-complexity keywords, context size, and remaining budget. These sit at BFS depth 2 — one hop past the governance and worker-pool spine.

tour.title: Streaming Results Back
tour.description: The final leg of the request lifecycle is getting output to the caller. websocket.py accepts WebSocket connections, routes chat and agentic-task messages, re-enforces budgets per message, streams incremental responses and execution events as they arrive from the worker pool, and computes per-message cost. This closes the spine that began at main.py: entry → router → governance → worker-pool subprocess → stream back, giving clients live token-by-token output instead of a single blocking response.

tour.title: Client Library & CLI Tooling
tour.description: CCA is consumed, not just served. The Python client library (claude_code_client barrel plus the synchronous ClaudeClient, fan-in 7) wraps the REST surface with complete/stream/batch/get_usage/health methods, context-manager lifecycle, and retry-with-backoff. The Typer CLI (claude_api.py) assembles sub-command groups on top of api_client.py's typed HTTP wrapper and utils.py's Rich-based formatting helpers (fan-in 13 — every command imports them). These are separate dependency trees from the service spine, which is why a forward import-walk from main.py never reaches them; their importance shows up instead as high fan-in within their own layers.

tour.title: Containerization, Deployment & CI
tour.description: Finally, how the service from Steps 1–9 ships. The Dockerfile packages the FastAPI app into a runnable image and docker-compose.yml orchestrates it alongside its Redis dependency for local and integration runs. The GitHub Actions pipelines automate the lifecycle: ci.yml runs the test suite on every change while deploy-staging.yml promotes builds. Together they turn the code you've toured into a deployable, continuously-tested unit — the operational envelope around a subprocess-driven LLM gateway.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers (push, pull_request) to launch `jobs`, each a sequence of `steps`; docker-compose's `depends_on` orders service startup so the API container waits for Redis before accepting traffic.
